title: onprem-airgap-offline-bundle: vendor rke2 + flatcar artifacts and add vendoring pipeline
author: Ravi Shah
description:
Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in highly regulated environments requested first-class support for RKE2 and Flatcar in our air-gapped installer. This PR adds vendored Helm charts, container image relayers, and offline-bundle generation changes to produce distro-specific bundles for RKE2 and Flatcar. The change also introduces a small vendoring pipeline (scripts + Make targets) that captures upstream artifacts and normalizes them into our offline bundle layout.

What changed (high level): vendored upstream Helm charts for ingress, cert-manager, and our runtime operator; added container-image manifests and relayer metadata for RKE2/Flatcar; updated offline-bundle builder to include an additional variant (rke2-flatcar); added smoke e2e install job that runs in our internal airgap test lab; documented upgrade/rollback notes and verifier checks for bundle integrity.

Compatibility: where possible this is additive and does not change existing ubuntu/ubuntu-kubeadm bundles. The installer selects the appropriate bundle variant based on detected kube-distro and node OS label. There is a small behavioral change in how the installer handles containerd config for Flatcar (documented) — customers should run the included preflight and verifier before upgrading.

Testing: unit tests for the bundle manifest generator, integration smoke tests in the airgap lab for fresh installs and upgrades (v1.3.2 -> v1.3.3), and manual verification of image relayer outputs. CI: all packaging and lint checks passed; the airgap-lab smoke job is run as a gated job post-merge.

Rollout: squash-merge to main. Ops/Platform will stage the bundles to the downloads CDN and notify the SRE oncall to seed the internal airgap mirror. See linked Linear ENG-8342 for rollout tracking.
